rows.stewards_excuse: When questioned Z Purton stated that the intention was to go forward. He said after being loaded into the starting gates APEX GLORY was fractious and as the start was effected bounded and lost ground. He said after being positioned at the back of the field he intended to ride the horse with cover behind SHANDONG SPIRIT, however, APEX GLORY raced keenly and refused to settle. He said as a result when BRING ME HOME improved three wide near the 900 Metres he was obliged to follow that runner, however, APEX GLORY continued to race keenly during the middle stages. He added after entering the Home Straight he improved to the outside of BRING ME HOME but his mount responded only fairly to his riding and, in his opinion, was particularly disappointing over the final 200 Metres when it commenced to give ground. Trainer K L Man stated the horse was disadvantaged by losing ground at the start and also racing too keenly. A warning was placed on the barrier manners of APEX GLORY. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings. The performance of APEX GLORY, a last start winner, was considered disappointing. Before being allowed to race again, APEX GLORY will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination. Sent for sampling post-race.

rows.stewards_excuse: Prior to the running of the event Trainer M Newnham confirmed that he had instructed L Ferraris to ride the horse in a conservative manner in the early stages to offset the wide barrier. From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages. When questioned L Ferraris confirmed that the instructions were to settle back in the field. He said after following PROFESSIONAL LAD during the event he considered improving between PROFESSIONAL LAD and PANACEA making the Home Turn. He said when PROFESSIONAL LAD shifted out leaving the 500 Metres to improve he then elected to improve to the inside of PROFESSIONAL LAD. He added after making ground near the 400 Metres he then was not able to place full vigour to his mount as he was concerned that PERFECTDAY, which was giving ground, may shift in and interfere with his mount and therefore he was required to ride with caution between the 400 Metres and the 250 Metres. He said when PERFECTDAY shifted out whilst giving ground near the 250 Metres his mount became slightly unbalanced when bumped by PERFECTDAY after which he was able to apply full pressure to TAGLINE. He added TAGLINE finished the race off well, however, he was of the opinion his mount may also have appreciated the surface with more give in it.
rows.note: official: ridden with caution about 400-250m behind giving-ground Perfectday and slightly unbalanced when bumped by Perfectday near 250m (not visually confirmable from this angle); made late ground for 6th
